hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
hook.sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
hook.line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
hook.translation: With these seemingly mixed words you confuse my mind. Tell me decisively that one thing by which I may reach the highest good.
hook.why: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasang.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
alternates.sanskrit: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
alternates.line: I can't tell which is better, or even what winning would look like.
alternates.translation: Nor do we know which is better for us, to fight or not, or whether we will win or they will. The very people after whose death we would not wish to live stand facing us.
alternates.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verse.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
verse.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: The self is not the roles you play; when you act from who you are, your duty is not a burden but your own nature.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.for_you: Do your own duty as an offering, from the self rather than from fear or pressure, and leave the rest to the divine.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verse.sanskrit: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
verse.line: Don't churn your mind with plans and second thoughts. Be still and rest in yourself.
verse.translation: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.

words.en: in the form of bliss of own true self

verse.why: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.
verse.misuse: Not a reason to avoid decisions; decide, then stop churning.

prasang.title: You are not your mind
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra drives home that Janaka is not the body, the doer, or the mind's likes and dislikes, but the ocean in which the waves of life rise and fall. He urges faith, an end to grief, and rest from endless deliberation.
prasang.lesson: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

verse.for_you: Ask what is right, not what is easy; choose your own duty with a clear mind and carry it out without fear.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि / पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् / न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभा- / द्धर्मं जह्याज्जीविस्यापि हेतोः
verse.line: Never give up what is right, not for desire, not from fear, not for money.
verse.translation: Here is the highest thing I can tell you, the purest and most valuable: never abandon what is right, not out of desire, not out of fear, not out of greed, not even to save your life.
verse.why: Don't trade what's right for desire, fear or money. Only your deeds stay with you.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: never abandon what is right
prasang.summary: Vidura closes with the heart of his counsel: never give up what is right for desire, fear or greed; only our deeds go with us; ask the wise when unsure.
prasang.lesson: Don't trade what's right for desire, fear or money. Only your deeds stay with you.

verse.for_you: You're pulled between two things that both feel right, and you've been carrying the choice alone.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् । स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
verse.line: Dropping a duty just because it's hard or you fear the strain isn't freedom. It gains you nothing.
verse.translation: One who gives up work because it is painful, out of fear of bodily strain, performs rajasic renunciation and does not gain its fruit.

words.en: due to fear of bodily pain

verse.why: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.
verse.misuse: Not 'never quit'. Leaving for good reasons is wise; this warns against fleeing out of fear alone.

prasang.title: What true renunciation is
prasang.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasang.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.
